top_cited_works.title: Dual-pump vibrational/rotational femtosecond/picosecond coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering temperature and species measurements
top_cited_works.abstract: A method for simultaneous ro-vibrational and pure-rotational hybrid femtosecond/picosecond coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (fs/ps CARS) is presented for multi-species detection and improved temperature sensitivity from room temperature to flame conditions. N₂/CH₄ vibrational and N₂/O₂/H₂ rotational Raman coherences are excited simultaneously using fs pump pulses at 660 and 798 nm, respectively, and a common fs Stokes pulse at 798 nm. A fourth narrowband 798 nm ps pulse probes all coherence states at a time delay that minimizes nonresonant background and the effects of collisions. The transition strength is concentration dependent, while the distribution among observed transitions is related to temperature through the Boltzmann distribution. The broadband excitation pulses and multiplexed signal are demonstrated for accurate thermometry from 298 to 2400 K and concentration measurements of four key combustion species.

top_cited_works.title: Non-Intrusive Measurement Techniques for Flow Characterization of Hypersonic Wind Tunnels
top_cited_works.venue: NASA STI Repository (National Aeronautics and Space Administration)
top_cited_works.abstract: This manuscript describes the wide variety of optical measurement techniques for characterizing the flow in hypersonic wind tunnels. The introduction briefly describes different types of hypersonic wind tunnels, why they are used, and typical freestream conditions including fluctuating quantities. Description of these conditions defines the challenge for measurement techniques which have varying degrees of accuracy and precision, and work only in certain temperature, density and/or speed regimes. The rest of the manuscript is broken up into sections, by measurement technique. Each technique is described and then several examples are provided. The concluding chapter compares and contrasts different aspects of the measurement techniques including accuracy, precision, spatial resolution and temporal resolution.

top_cited_works.title: Single-shot ultrafast coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering of vibrational/rotational nonequilibrium
top_cited_works.abstract: The study of internal molecular energy transfer is important for a variety of nonequilibrium and nonthermal environments, including plasma-based manufacturing and materials treatment, medical device treatment applications, and plasma-assisted combustion. In the current work, hybrid femtosecond/picosecond coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering spectroscopy is demonstrated for simultaneous, single-shot measurement of pure-rotational and rovibrational energy distributions in the highly nonequilibrium environment of a dielectric barrier discharge plasma. Detailed spatial distributions and shot-to-shot fluctuations of rotational temperatures spanning 325–450 K and corresponding vibrational temperatures of 1200–5000 K are recorded across the plasma and surrounding flow with high precision and accuracy. This approach allows concise measurements of vibrational/rotational energy distributions in nonequilibrium environments at kilohertz rates that are free of nonresonant background and minimize interference from molecular collisions.

Application of an optical emission spectroscopy sensor design to a dual-mode scramjet flowpath
recent_works.abstract: Abstract The feasibility of using optical emission spectroscopy (OES) sensors in dual-mode scramjet engines has been demonstrated previously, but the technology is not yet mature. The main weakness in previous studies has been the reliance on sensitivities specific to sensor locations in a flowpath geometry. To address this, this work presents the design of a custom OES sensor and its application in a dual-mode scramjet geometry. Light collection was implemented in an orientation that matches what is achievable in axisymmetric flowpath geometries, viewing into a flameholding cavity as opposed to across it (direct-cavity angle). A multi-anode photomultiplier tube (MAPMT) detector was used in the OES sensor design, which provided increased light sensitivity and the ability to use multiple channels to resolve spatial or spectral information. The OES sensor implemented a transmission grating to disperse OH* and CH* flame chemiluminescence onto discrete anodes of the detector. Experiments in a dual-mode scramjet facility demonstrated that the sensor was sensitive to changes in flowpath conditions from a variety of axial positions. recent_works.title: Laser Absorption Spectroscopy Measurements of Air Mass Flow Rate in a Model Scramjet Isolator via Ambient CO 2
recent_works.abstract: This manuscript describes the application of a two-color mid-infrared laser absorption spectroscopy (LAS) diagnostic providing measurements of air temperature, pressure, velocity, and mass flow rate at 300 kHz via ambient CO2. The diagnostic was applied in the isolator of a model scramjet within the University of Virginia Supersonic Combustion Facility (UVASCF). The measurements were achieved by scanning the wavelength of two interband cascade lasers (ICLs) across multiple absorption lines ofCO2 near 2375 and 2384 cm−1. The use of mid-infrared wavelengths provides large absorption signals in air despite the relatively small concentration of CO2. The mass flow rate measurements in the UVASCF isolator agree reasonably well with theoretical predictions over a range of plenum temperatures and pressures, and demonstrate the characterization of internal scramjet flows via flight-capable optical hardware. This is notable compared to our prior measurements acquired behind incident shock waves in a shock tube due to the presence of relatively thick boundary layers (≈1/3 of path length) in the scramjet isolator.

recent_works.title: Spanwise OH PLIF Visualization of Flame Structure and Location in a Dual-Mode Scramjet Combustor
recent_works.abstract: Hydroxyl radical planar laser-induced fluorescence (OH PLIF) images were acquired over a dense array of spanwise measurement planes for an ethylene-fueled dual-mode scramjet cavity flameholder in the University of Virginia Supersonic Combustion Facility (UVASCF). Two fueling conditions were investigated: the first, using injectors located in the isolator; the second, using injectors located at the diverging wall just upstream of the cavity step. From these images, the three-dimensional volume of the flame intermittency for each condition was interpolated, revealing differences in spanwise structures between the two conditions. These results provide insight previously unavailable in similar facilities regarding the role of spanwise effects on the flame stabilization mechanism, which is typically imaged at the facility centerline. Implications for interpolating both path-integrated and centerline experimental data are discussed.

recent_works.title: CUBRC 48” Tunnel Hypersonic Ground Testing of NOSpec
recent_works.abstract: Active control of hypersonic vehicles is a current area of research and development. Measurement of external flows around these vehicles can potentially be used as feedback for a control algorithm. To this end, a novel optical emission spectroscopy (OES) sensor called NOSpec was tested in the CUBRC LENS 48-inch reflected shock tunnel. NOSpec is a fiber coupled sensor utilizing a multi-anode photomultiplier tube array (MAPMT) as the detector to examine the external flow over a hypersonic vehicle. A blunt wedge with rounded corners and 10º half angle was used as the flight vehicle geometry for testing with a window placed on the blunt edge and a fiber collimator behind the window. These tests detected a noticeable change in NO signal from 0º angle of attack to 10º or 20º angle of attack while collecting information about the flow field. This work demonstrates the feasibility of the novel sensor architecture to non-intrusively detect changes in angle of attack, and it may be applied in the future for hypersonic vehicle active control.
